title: Introduce localized admission tamer and graceful escort for soft shedding
author: Maya Thompson
description: Motivation: recent regional latency spikes caused aggressive circuit opens and tenant evictions that degraded customer experience. Existing load-shedding reacted to healthy-appearing signals too coarsely and lacked a localized slowpath that can softly trim admission without full eviction. This PR introduces an 'admission tamer' layer coupled with a lightweight 'graceful escort' to manage inflight requests for tenants during transient overloads. The design preserves SLOs by trading reduced concurrency for better p99 latency stability and avoids hard tenant quarantines where possible. Key features: 1) Localized soft-shedding policy that applies per-tenant per-zone admission limits derived from short-window latency histograms; 2) Circuit hint propagation so downstream routers can prefer compatible slowpath variants instead of hard-failing; 3) Graceful escort: an admission queue with time-bounded draining and hedged short-circuit fallback to prevent head-of-line stalls; 4) Telemetry hooks for tracing admission decisions and a new metric (admission_tamer_trim_rate) to drive rollouts; 5) Opt-in runtime flag to enable staged rollout by region. This PR includes unit/integration tests, a small load test harness, and updated docs for the operator flags. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (https://linear.app/ENG/4182/admission-tamer-localized-soft-shedding) - [x] Implementation of runtime admission tamer - [x] Circuit hint propagation and header mapping - [x] Telemetry + dashboards (skeleton) - [x] Tests (unit + integration) - [x] Feature flag + rollout notes Impact: should reduce p99 latency spikes from tenant-driven surges and reduce hard-evictions observed during previous incidents. Rollout plan: enable in a canary region for 48h with observability thresholds before global rollout.

notes: This change was driven by incident 2026-01-27 where region us-east-1 experienced a tenant surge that cascaded through kv warmups. The admission tamer is conservative by default and disabled in global config until canary completes. Ops can instantly disable via feature flag and the gateway will stop propagating circuit-hints if disabled.
